entries.summary: Before building a game, the trainer was tested on a StarCraft micro benchmark: 0.99 win rate vs the reference's 0.38. Later failures are the game's.
entries.title: Check the PPO trainer against a reference (M0/M1)

entries.summary: Built a 24x24 top-down shooter with walls, vision cones, fog and team radar. Fair (random vs random 0.497) and fast (1.5-3.7M agent-steps/s).
entries.title: The arena: a grid shooter in pure JAX (M2)

entries.summary: Choosing move, turn and fire separately plus a higher learning rate took agents from 22% to ~0.8-0.9 wins against a scripted rusher.
entries.title: First learning: factored action head + lr 1e-3 (M3)

entries.summary: Self-play agents beat bot-trained agents 0.58-0.69 but only 0.77 vs a simple rusher: teams split into lone duelists that get caught 2-on-1.
entries.title: First self-play (M4)

entries.summary: Plain self-play (latest self only) was best and most consistent (0.72 vs the rusher); 4 of 10 pool/PFSP seeds got stuck at 0.5.
entries.title: Naive vs pool vs PFSP self-play (Exp A)

entries.metric: head-to-head win rate vs other recipes
entries.summary: 20% scripted-bot games won everything (0.63-0.64 head to head, 0.78-0.88 vs unseen bot styles); a co-trained exploiter added nothing.
entries.title: 20% scripted bots mixed into self-play (Exp R)

entries.summary: First-person observations were ahead of north-up by 0.05-0.12 vs every bot (3 seeds each, ranges overlap). Kept first-person.
entries.title: First-person vs north-up observations

entries.metric: MAPPO head-to-head win rate vs IPPO
entries.summary: MAPPO teams grouped up and got shot from the side by spread-out IPPO pairs, scoring only 0.37 head to head. IPPO kept.
entries.title: IPPO vs MAPPO (shared critic)

entries.metric: win rate when team info removed
entries.summary: Agents strafe on purpose, use teammates' info (removing it costs 0.09-0.15), and one rating per agent predicts matchups within ~0.03.
entries.title: Diagnostics: strafing, team info, transitivity (M6)

entries.summary: Added target choice, reaction time, footsteps through walls, silent walk, flicks, 5v5 and bomb mode, each a switch; 73% of generated maps pass fairness.
entries.title: CS-like mechanics behind switches (M8)

entries.metric: share of shots fired while moving
entries.summary: No regression and sampled vs greedy play now agree, but agents still fire 23% of shots on the move: the game rule makes strafing rational.
entries.title: Autoregressive action head + decaying randomness (M7)

entries.summary: 19 scripted playbooks showed bomb mode rewards coordinated attack (+0.15, sound alone +0.18) while elimination never rewards teamwork. Bomb mode kept.
entries.title: Does the game reward teamwork? Playbook audit (M9)

entries.metric: share of shots fired while moving
entries.summary: Making running shots 4x less accurate left scripted results identical; the learned pilot later fired only 3.9% of shots while moving (was 22%).
entries.title: CS-like running inaccuracy x0.25 (D6)

entries.summary: The first bomb-mode agent learned (0 to ~0.6 vs playbooks). Its replays exposed scripted defenders stuck in a narrow gap; fixed, 5-7% to <1%.
entries.title: Bomb-mode pilot learns; replays reveal a playbook traffic jam

entries.metric: win rate vs scripted playbooks per side
entries.summary: Split by side, the agent attacked better than any playbook (0.81-0.87) but defended worse than a plain scripted rush (0.42-0.48).
entries.title: Pilot scored per side: strong attack, weak defense

entries.summary: Timings were inside CS ranges, and giving defenders more plant time left attackers at 0.56. Time was not the bottleneck; fights were.
entries.title: Is bomb mode unfair to defenders? Timing calibration

entries.summary: No rock-paper-scissors cycling: attackers split sites evenly and later checkpoints beat earlier ones. Learned defenders rarely sit on sites.
entries.title: Pilot analyses: no strategy cycling (M12)

entries.metric: duel win rate with 1-tick head start
entries.summary: Faster fire moved balance toward 50/50 and a one-tick head start won 67-98% of duels; a 45-degree crosshair rule gave holders an edge.
entries.title: Lethality audit: fire rate, ordered fire, crosshair rule (M13)

entries.summary: A regroup-and-retake playbook helped a little; scripted grenades and an aim-settle rule did not change the game's structure for bots.
entries.title: Group-rotate defense, scripted grenades, aim settle

entries.metric: defense teamwork premium vs solo bots
entries.summary: Against truly solo bots organized defense gains ~10 points. Flick shots make a pre-aimed holder win ~70%, roughly like CS off-angles.
entries.title: Real no-teamwork yardstick and flick shots

entries.metric: pilot attack win rate vs scripted defenses
entries.summary: D7 = fast fire + ordered fire + crosshair + flicks. The old agent's attack fell from 0.77 to 0.16-0.43: the rules matter for learners.
entries.title: D7 game chosen; the D6 pilot collapses in it

entries.summary: Exploiter copies trained 2e7 steps gained only +0.01 per side: no cheap holes (at lr 1e-3 the copy got worse instead).
entries.title: First exploiter robustness check

entries.summary: A rewrite made training 1.58x faster with identical gradients; runs that looked finished gained +0.06 per side once the learning rate stopped hitting zero.
entries.title: Exact action-head rewrite; plateau was the LR schedule

entries.metric: T win rate vs that defense
entries.summary: A copy trained only against the toughest scripted defense rose 0.52 to 0.65 on all 4 seeds: the network can do it, self-play just never shows it.
entries.title: Best response vs the share-and-collapse defense

entries.summary: Computing only the taken branch of the action head trained 31% faster; a 4-seed paired test showed no significant quality loss.
entries.title: Taken-branch action head (+31% speed)

entries.summary: 'Losing to past selves' was a logging bug; the real decline came from pool mode training on half the data per update. Batch-matched, pool beat naive.
entries.title: Pool self-play decline: logging bug + half data per update

entries.metric: T win rate vs held-out defenses
entries.summary: Training against scripted plans improved attack even against held-out defenses (+0.03/+0.05 on 2 seeds); defense was mixed.
entries.title: 20% scripted plans in D7 training (2 seeds)

entries.summary: At equal steps, doubling parallel games was slightly worse because it halves the number of updates.
entries.title: 1024 vs 512 parallel games for naive self-play

entries.summary: No exploiter found a real hole; a random-init exploiter won 0 rounds in 79M steps because it never planted and got no learning signal.
entries.title: Stronger and cold-start exploiters

entries.summary: A specialist gains +0.08 to +0.14 against any fixed scripted defense, so the 'blind spot' was just the strongest style, not a trick.
entries.title: The blind spot is a normal specialization premium

entries.summary: A 10-agent round robin became the main yardstick: agents within ~60 Elo, and the bot ladder and head-to-head strength disagreed.
entries.title: First round-robin tournament with Bradley-Terry Elo

entries.metric: defense win rate, average and worst case
entries.summary: Learned defense matched the best scripted defense on average but was more robust (worst case ~0.5 vs <=0.43); learned attack beat all scripts.
entries.title: Scripted baseline on held-out ladder maps

entries.summary: Teaching the network to predict where hidden enemies are did not help: -1 and -18 Elo on two seeds.
entries.title: Privileged belief head (predict hidden enemies)

entries.summary: Giving agents a wallhack lifted defense by +0.18 and attack by nothing: defenders lack information, attackers already know where sites are.
entries.title: Wallhack ceiling: perfect enemy information

entries.summary: Training against a pool of 9 other agents improved results vs bot styles (+0.02-0.035) at no cost; head-to-head strength unchanged (+3/0 Elo).
entries.title: League-lite: pool seeded with 9 trained agents

entries.summary: Training only against bots reached 0.80 vs bots, even unseen plans, but was 122 Elo weaker against learned agents.
entries.title: One policy trained only against scripted plans

entries.summary: Best agents win 100% vs very early checkpoints, falling smoothly with opponent skill; even weak learners take 27-31% of rounds.
entries.title: Skill gradient vs weaker learned agents

entries.summary: Telling the network which scripted plan it faced added nothing (0.797 vs 0.815): one policy already beats all plans at once.
entries.title: Plan-ID ceiling: tell the network which plan it faces

entries.summary: A GRU over the round's history predicted hidden enemies only ~1% better than the current observation. GRU policies built but never trained.
entries.title: Memory probes: does round history find hidden enemies?

entries.summary: 50% bot games bought +0.14 defense vs bots for ~-12 Elo; a bot flag did not remove the trade-off (-21 Elo). Kept 20%.
entries.title: Bot share 35/50% and a 'this is a bot' flag

entries.summary: Benchmarks showed RTX PRO 6000 / L40S at $0.19 per billion steps vs $0.33 for H100; one CPU core and 8 GiB suffice.
entries.title: Cheapest cloud GPU setup

entries.metric: head-to-head win rate wide vs normal
entries.summary: Doubling the trained network's width in place gave no gain (0.488 head to head, 1 seed) and ran at 0.6x speed.
entries.title: 2x wider network by surgical widening

entries.summary: Each 2e8-step league block still added strength (+34, then +12 Elo); matched plain self-play gained only +8 vs league's +31.
entries.title: Longer league-lite training vs plain self-play

entries.summary: Every run now logs its timing; caching navigation fields cut env build from 18.6 s to 0.3 s.
entries.title: Overhead accounting and startup speed-ups

entries.summary: Agents learned never to throw: early throws landed where they walked next and burned the thrower (365 self ticks vs 16 on enemies).
entries.title: Molotov thrown along the facing (D8)

entries.metric: Elo main effect of 2x data per update
entries.summary: Of LR anneal, clip 0.1, 2x data per update and PFSP, all effects were small; 2x data per update was adopted for being 23% faster at no loss.
entries.title: Factorial of 4 PPO knobs

entries.summary: Half-precision matrix math trained 1.32x faster with equal quality (+2 vs -5 Elo); with the new batch recipe 1.52x overall.
entries.title: FP16 matmuls on the laptop

entries.summary: The policy network was healthy (0-0.8% dormant units); the critic slowly lost units. On open maps the straight line to a site was nearly always right.
entries.title: Plasticity probe and map openness check

entries.summary: Free throws first, then real friendly fire: agents kept only useful throws and gained +49 Elo, the biggest head-to-head jump so far (1 seed).
entries.title: Aimed molotovs with a two-stage curriculum

entries.summary: Fights start ~9 tiles away, beyond the agents' 5-tile wall view; 73% of rounds end by elimination before any plant.
entries.title: Where rounds are decided

entries.summary: A coarse map view out to 10 tiles was used a little by the network but did not improve play (+8 vs +7 Elo).
entries.title: Far view: coarse walls to 10 tiles

entries.summary: On a big cloud GPU, training is almost all game simulation; BF16 adds 1.7%. 1e8 steps cost about $0.10 of GPU time.
entries.title: Cloud benchmark of the current recipe

entries.summary: Stage 3 reached +79 Elo, then plateaued; a second seed was slower but reached +45 (seed 0 +66 in the same tournament).
entries.title: Molotov line: stages 3-4 and a second seed

entries.summary: Smokes first cost strength, then gave +20..+31 Elo on one seed but about -9 on another. Kept as an option, not in the main line.
entries.title: Smoke grenades for attackers

entries.summary: Training moved to a desktop GTX 1660 Ti (later also a friend's RTX 2080 Ti) with a job queue that survives disconnects.
entries.title: Desktop GPU wired up; laptop retired

entries.summary: A 50x50 world would make training 2.3x slower per decision and ~4x per round of experience. Stayed at 28x28.
entries.title: Cost of a finer 50x50 grid

entries.metric: attack win rate vs bots on CS maps
entries.summary: Agents winning ~82% vs bots on open maps won only 12-21% on real CS layouts: 'robustly strong' was an open-map result.
entries.title: Zero-shot on CS maps: best agents collapse

entries.summary: Dust2, Mirage, Inferno, Ancient and Anubis on the 28x28 grid: far tighter than our maps (1-tile chokes, 2.3-tile sightlines). Mirage held out.
entries.title: Five CS maps translated from CS2 radars

entries.summary: Training on 4 real maps gained +251 Elo there, but more training made the unseen Mirage worse (+72 to +41): memorization.
entries.title: Training on 4 real CS maps: fast, then memorization

entries.metric: failed move share on CS maps
entries.summary: Agents facing diagonally in 1-tile corridors could not move at all (42-67% of moves failed); letting moves slide along walls cut time-outs 58% to 16%.
entries.title: Wall sliding: half of all moves failed on CS maps

entries.summary: A CS-like map generator taught play that transfers to real maps never seen, and kept improving on Mirage where 4 real maps declined.
entries.title: Train on generated CS-like maps only

entries.metric: Elo on unseen Mirage vs 4-real-map agent
entries.summary: With wall sliding, the generated-map agent beat the agent trained on 4 real maps by ~70 Elo on unseen Mirage, on 2 seeds.
entries.title: Slide + generated maps beat 4 real maps on unseen map

entries.summary: Grenades aimed at entrances and chokes matter ~4x more on CS maps for bots; learned agents adopted smokes, dropped molotovs, +7..+9 Elo (1 seed).
entries.title: Utility spots and smoke-legs rule

entries.metric: Elo on 5 CS maps vs attacker-only arm
entries.summary: Letting defenders smoke, as in CS, improved defense by 0.04-0.05 (+24 vs +6 Elo on CS maps, 1 seed). Adopted.
entries.title: Defender smokes (both sides smoke)

entries.summary: Quadrupling the exploration bonus cost 9-12 Elo on both seeds; entropy sat where the game wanted it.
entries.title: Higher entropy bonus

entries.metric: Elo on 5 CS maps vs control
entries.summary: Telling agents the first step along the shortest path to each site gave a small, consistent +10 Elo on both seeds at 2% cost.
entries.title: Path compass observation

entries.metric: Elo on Mirage vs full bank
entries.summary: Training only on the 717 balanced maps of 2,048 made agents worse on both seeds: variety beat balance.
entries.title: Side-balanced subset of generated maps

entries.summary: 16-bit buffers gave no speed-up; they let 2,048 games fit in memory but at +18% cost per step. Shelved.
entries.title: 16-bit rollout storage and 2,048 games per update

entries.summary: Spending 30% of rounds on hold/retake drills barely helped defense (+0.01) and cost 18-24 Elo on the unseen map.
entries.title: Start-state curriculum (hold / retake drills)

entries.summary: Widening in place gave a small single-seed gain (+5/+10 Elo) at 21% more time per step: about what extra training buys.
entries.title: Surgical widening to 256 on the compass line

entries.summary: Teammates' observations added nothing to value prediction (bar +0.03): the shared team memory already carries it. Not built.
entries.title: Team-information critic probe

entries.metric: exploiter gain vs its attack (1e8 steps)
entries.summary: The best agent beat every earlier line (worst matchup 0.55), but a dedicated 1e8-step exploiter found a moderate hole in its attack (+0.05).
entries.title: Exploitability and style panel of the best agent

entries.summary: After ~8e8 steps agents rediscovered molotovs and jumped to ~+155 Elo; two seeds climbed the same way and stopped at the same level.
entries.title: Main line: late utility jump, then a fixed point

entries.summary: A tool scores hundreds of rounds and renders the best, worst and most wasteful ones as GIFs; even top agents lose quick rounds to weak ones.
entries.title: Round GIFs: best, worst and wasted-utility rounds

entries.summary: History still added nothing over the hand-built memory. A fair tracker without true identities would mislabel about 1 in 8 re-sightings.
entries.title: Memory probe v3 and a fair identity tracker

entries.summary: Checking outside research claims: the PPO clip bound only 1.3% of samples (KL 0.0012), so step size is set by the learning rate.
entries.title: PPO clip almost never binds

entries.summary: Making heard enemies anonymous, as in CS, cost nothing measurable on two seeds. Candidate default.
entries.title: Anonymous sounds (identity tracker)

entries.metric: Elo vs plain control (clip 0.1, seed-paired, CS maps)
entries.summary: None of the PPO knobs restarted learning; plain continuation still gained ~+14 Elo per block, so the earlier 'flat' was noise.
entries.title: Plateau test: bigger batch, clip 0.1, 1 epoch, no value clip

entries.summary: A fresh network nudged toward the teacher for 5e7 steps never copied it (0.61 vs 0.86 vs bots): far too few gradient updates.
entries.title: On-policy distillation into a fresh network

entries.summary: Trained from random weights for 1.4e9 steps, attackers never won a round: a random attacker almost never plants, so there is no signal.
entries.title: From-scratch rerun in today's game

entries.summary: Added CS-style HE grenades (damage falloff) and flashbangs (blindness by view angle), off by default, with 49 tests and bots that use them.
entries.title: HE grenades and flashbangs built

entries.summary: Search found +4% win probability per decision only when it knew hidden enemy positions; with fair beliefs the gain vanished (+0.2%).
entries.title: Search headroom: oracle vs fair beliefs

entries.summary: Same recipe, different seed: 11-21 Elo apart, while tournaments are honest to ~3-4 Elo. Rule adopted: two seeds per arm, compared seed-paired.
entries.title: Noise calibration: seeds dominate

entries.metric: Elo vs tracker-only control at 4e8 (CS maps)
entries.summary: Realistic sounds cost up to 23 Elo while agents adapted, then broke even or gained after 4e8 steps. Lesson: judge rule changes at 4e8.
entries.title: Throw, plant, defuse sounds and merged footsteps

entries.metric: Elo vs original after 4e8 (CS maps, pooled)
entries.summary: A fresh copy of the best agent first looked ~1.5x faster to learn; re-measured on 2 seeds the edge shrank to ~+10 on CS maps, ~0 on Mirage.
entries.title: Supervised copy into a fresh same-width network

entries.summary: Swapping in a fresh critic did nothing (-1/+0 Elo), though a third of the old critic's layer-2 units were nearly dead.
entries.title: Fresh critic only

entries.metric: Elo vs same-budget original (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: Copying the best agent into a fresh network twice as wide, then training, beat the original by ~40 Elo on two seeds. Main line went wide.
entries.title: Distil into a 2x wider fresh network

entries.metric: enemy firing lines cut minus own lines cut, per smoke
entries.summary: Counting firing lines, smokes blocked the agents' own shots as often as the enemy's; molotovs hurt enemies 3-8x more than teammates.
entries.title: Productive-utility measure: smokes are a wash

entries.summary: A 512-wide copy gained +18 on CS maps but +2 on Mirage (1 seed) at twice the cost: diminishing returns.
entries.title: 512-wide fresh copy

entries.metric: Elo vs no-HE control (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: Added plainly, agents never threw HE. With a free-damage stage first they kept throwing under real rules and gained +8 Elo on two seeds.
entries.title: HE: plain warm start never throws; free curriculum works

entries.summary: Training alongside exploiters gave a small two-seed gain (+7/+13 Elo) but did not make the agent harder to exploit.
entries.title: Co-trained warm exploiters in the league

entries.metric: Elo vs wide line (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: Stacking the wide network, realistic sound, HE and exploiters gave +33 Elo over 4e8 steps on two seeds; parts not isolated.
entries.title: Main line: wide + sound + HE + exploiters

entries.metric: Elo vs control at 6e8 (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: The free stage taught agents to flash freely; under real rules they kept blinding themselves (3.1 ticks per flash) and lost 13 Elo.
entries.title: Flashbangs with the free curriculum

entries.summary: Scripted bots do throw HE, but only at stacked enemies: ~0.04 per bot-round vs ~0.35 per agent-round, so agents rarely faced HE.
entries.title: Correction: bots throw HE ~8x less than agents

entries.summary: Exploiter-trained agents were as exploitable as before (+0.039 vs +0.043 win rate for a dedicated exploiter); both small.
entries.title: Does exploiter training reduce exploitability?

entries.summary: Flags worth 2.3x on CPU did nothing on GPU; profiling showed game resets were the real cost. The units layer (finer worlds) was kept.
entries.title: Trainer speed flags and units layer (res-units)

entries.summary: The usage script counted throws in unfinished rounds; all per-round grenade counts were 10-20% too high. Elo numbers unaffected.
entries.title: Correction: grenade usage inflated 10-20%

entries.metric: Elo gain of block 7 (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: Per-block gains shrank from ~+11-17 Elo to +3/-3 by block 7: the recipe plateaued after ~1.4e9 steps (best +153 over the 10-15 best).
entries.title: Main line blocks 2-7: diminishing returns to a plateau

entries.summary: Pre-building start states once per rollout made training 1.13-1.17x faster (1.62x in a 2x finer world) with unchanged metrics.
entries.title: Reset queue of pre-built start states

entries.summary: Copying the plateaued agent into a fresh network, same width or 512 wide, did not help (-8 and -7 Elo): the plateau is not capacity.
entries.title: Re-distillation at the plateau

entries.metric: Elo of agents trained vs v2 bots (CS maps)
entries.summary: Fixed bot pathing cut stuck time 51.6 to 7.3 ticks per round and made bots ~0.03-0.045 harder; training against them was Elo-neutral.
entries.title: Better bots: navigation v2 + HE bots v2

entries.metric: Elo gain of block 8 (CS maps, seed-paired)
entries.summary: Block 8 still gained +8/+7 Elo, so the plateau was not yet flat.
entries.title: Main line block 8

entries.summary: A 2-tick fuse lets teams dodge their own flashes; bots with flashes now win +3.3 points more rounds (was +1.8). Learner test pending.
entries.title: Flash v2: fuse, visible throws, smarter flash bots

entries.summary: Ray shooting merged (bots +0.035 rounds, 8.6% kills through smoke), but it slowed training 13% (gate 5%). RL A/B still running here.
entries.title: Ray shooting, magazines and point-fire bots

entries.summary: Block 9 beat block 8b by 13 Elo on CS maps (+7 on held-out Mirage); no plateau yet.
entries.title: Main line block 9 (first vs v2 bots)

entries.summary: Bullets as rays plus magazines: trained agents win the new game by 35 Elo and lose nothing in the old one; blind shots get 2-3x more accurate.
entries.title: Ray shooting + magazines

entries.summary: The non-ray line still gained +6 CS / +12 Mirage, but the ray line beat it by 35 at equal compute.
entries.title: Main line block 10 (no rays)

entries.summary: Turning off the co-trained exploiter made training 1.68x faster; the XLA flag gave nothing (1.00x).
entries.title: Exploiter time cost; XLA +WHILE flag

entries.summary: First ray main-line block: +10 CS / +16 Mirage over its parents.
entries.title: Ray main line block 1

entries.summary: No harm from the flash game, but agents stopped throwing flashes within ~1e8 steps because early flashes blinded themselves.
entries.title: Flash v2 stage-2 RL

entries.summary: After a crash, exploiter runs now resume bit-for-bit; until then no main-line run since 10-17 could resume.
entries.title: Exact resume for exploiter runs; queue restart

entries.summary: On the GPU the flash observation block cost as much as the bots' dodge; a CPU profile had said it was cheap.
entries.title: GPU flash cost attribution

entries.summary: Doubling the learning rate hurt: -10 CS, -33 Mirage.
entries.title: Learning rate 6e-4

entries.summary: Dropping the exploiter was rejected on a noisy Mirage -13; later re-judged as harmless on CS and dropped on 10-21.
entries.title: Drop co-trained exploiter (equal wall time)

entries.summary: Ray line gained +12, +12, +6, +5 per block: plateau by block 4-5.
entries.title: Ray line blocks 2-5 plateau

entries.summary: Bit-identical code fixes: 1.43x faster in the ray game, 2.55x in the flash game.
entries.title: Exact speed fixes (ray-speed)

entries.summary: Even free flashes went unused (0.004 per round): agents never learned to push a blinded enemy, so flashes had no payoff.
entries.title: Cost randomization for own grenades

entries.summary: Exploiter on half the games: 1.21x faster training and no loss at equal time.
entries.title: Cheaper exploiter (512 games)

entries.summary: Flash line gained +6, +7, then +4 CS / -6 Mirage: paused at block 2.
entries.title: Flash main line blocks 1-3

entries.summary: Enemies can now see a flying flash and hear a throw; flashes blind slightly less, bots unaffected.
entries.title: Flash fidelity: see flight, hear throw

entries.summary: Letting the critic see hidden enemies barely helped (+0.003 vs +0.03 needed): team memory already tells it where they are.
entries.title: Opponent-information critic probe

entries.summary: Cutting the learning rate to a third broke the plateau: +9 CS, +15 Mirage.
entries.title: Learning rate 1e-4 at plateau

entries.summary: Halving the rate again did nothing; the 1e-4 line gained +8 then plateaued (+4).
entries.title: lr 5e-5 arm; lr-1e-4 blocks 4-5

entries.summary: The kickstart turned flashing on for good, but agents threw both flashes every round and mostly blinded themselves.
entries.title: Flash-combo v1: bot kickstart, assist shaping

entries.summary: After fixing a bug the bot check exposed, agents halved shooting on the move and got slightly better even in the old game.
entries.title: Fight dynamics: tagging, moving accuracy

entries.summary: Extra residual layers added nothing and cost 15-27% speed: capacity is not the limit.
entries.title: Residual blocks (depth)

entries.summary: New realism game: +13 in block 1 (adapting), then +3 in block 2.
entries.title: FX game blocks 1-2

entries.summary: Agents looked unexploitable, but the probe trained at 3x the agent's learning rate and damaged itself.
entries.title: Warm-exploiter probe reads 'unexploitable'

entries.summary: Per-round buy tiers adopted: no harm, and eco teams rush sites and take closer fights.
entries.title: Eco-lite loadout tiers

entries.summary: Lowering the learning rate during a block beat a constant rate by +4 CS / +7 Mirage.
entries.title: lr anneal within a block

entries.summary: A two-sided kick gave moderate flashing (0.1 per round) at no Elo cost, though throwers still blind themselves.
entries.title: Flash-combo v2: two-sided kick

entries.summary: FX + tiers block 1 gained +6 and became best; plain block 2 added 0.
entries.title: FX + tiers line blocks 1-2

entries.summary: Agents walk 7-15% of the time vs bots' 42%, give themselves away, and their silent approaches don't pay.
entries.title: Walk audit

entries.summary: On the main line the flash kick cost 9 Elo on CS maps; the user dropped it.
entries.title: Flash kick on the main line

entries.summary: Forcing agents to walk near enemies cost 79 Elo: it wrecked their timing.
entries.title: Walk-override probe

entries.summary: The 'exploiter' sat at 50% against the main agent all along; its benefit came from adding near-copies to the opponent pool.
entries.title: The co-trained exploiter never exploits

entries.summary: With one bomb carrier, agents planted under half as often as before and didn't relearn it in one block.
entries.title: Bomb carry, first try

entries.summary: A 2,200-test, 2.5-hour suite became a 465-test, 6-minute fast tier.
entries.title: Test-suite fast tier

entries.summary: One list of parked and ruled-out ideas; notebook timestamps that drifted up to 3.5 h were fixed.
entries.title: the parked list and notebook clock fix

entries.summary: Properly calibrated attackers find small, growing holes: up to 5 points of win rate after 2e8 steps.
entries.title: Calibrated exploitability probe (PR-1)

entries.summary: Pushing exploiters toward a scripted plan wiped their skill (score 0.5 -> 0.07); stopped at the pilot.
entries.title: Plan-kicked exploiters (PCX, PR-2)

entries.summary: A web replay viewer with vision cones, team memory, policy panels, what-if edits and heat maps.
entries.title: Replay viewer

entries.summary: Realistic stray bullets were harmless but unlearned: friendly fire costs too little to show in the reward.
entries.title: Stray fire and friendly fire

entries.summary: Replacing the co-trained exploiter with the block start in the pool lost nothing and trained 1.4x faster.
entries.title: Drop the exploiter for a pool entry (U2 Z, P0)

entries.summary: 16-bit merged policy heads: ~5% faster training, no harm.
entries.title: 16-bit merged-head learner

entries.summary: The holes pointed at the game: a generated-map geometry quirk and a flash about twice as strong as CS2's.
entries.title: Hole triage

entries.summary: Agents can no longer see behind themselves; ambush kills rise, balance stays.
entries.title: CS vision: no see-behind, 106-degree FOV

entries.summary: No-exploiter + 16-bit recipe matched the old recipe at ~1.4x speed.

entries.summary: With CS2-length flash blindness the exploiter's retake-flash trick stopped working.

entries.summary: Re-judging 34 experiments flipped 2 decisions, both already reversed in practice.
entries.title: Re-verdict of 34 past A/Bs

entries.metric: CS Elo vs old game's block 2

entries.summary: The speed flag costs nothing measurable and gives ~1.3x speed; kept.
entries.title: anchor_static speed flag check

entries.summary: Fresh attackers find only small holes (~1 point of win rate) in the newer agents.
entries.title: Exploit probes of new games

entries.summary: 66 pro maps: rifles hit 46% of bullets standing; a bug had credited kill shots to the wrong target.
entries.title: Pro CS2 data and the kill-shot bug

entries.summary: Training chunks alternate 12/14 s for no visible reason; fixing it would be worth ~10%.

entries.summary: Training on more CS-like generated maps gave +5 Elo on real CS maps across 4 seeds.
entries.title: Generator v2 CS-like maps

entries.summary: Worker PCs get a status tray; re-running a stopped job now continues it instead of overwriting.
entries.title: Worker tray and resume-on-rerun

entries.metric: CS Elo in own game, 2 blocks
entries.summary: Pro-calibrated shooting adopted: +4 in its own game, -6 in the old one (within the bar).
entries.title: CS2-calibrated shooting (cs v2)

entries.summary: 224 pro maps confirmed the shooting fit; a memory-aim tweak overshot smoke kills and was parked.
entries.title: 224 pro maps; cs3 memory aim

entries.summary: New game line gained +2, +3, +1: flat again.
entries.title: cs-shot line blocks 3-5

entries.summary: Economy and endgames already match pros; our rounds are twice as fast and grenades far too deadly.
entries.title: Pros vs our game, round by round

entries.summary: One full epoch plus one critic-only epoch: 7% faster training, no harm.
entries.title: PPG split (critic-only epoch)

entries.summary: Setting every parameter to pro values pushed the game toward defenders; only the grenade part went on.
entries.title: Full pro-calibration batch

entries.summary: Grenade damage set to pro levels: utility kills 7.5% -> 2.0%, +5 Elo at home, no harm.
entries.title: Grenade fix (utility-only procal)

entries.summary: Four blocks later, bomb-carry agents still plant half as often; tactics emerge slowly.
entries.title: Bomb carry retry, 4 blocks

entries.summary: A realistic money system was harmless and buys like pros, but agents never learned to save.
entries.title: Economy E1

entries.summary: Holders now win more duels; agents gained +20 adapting, but rounds stayed fast (9.6 s vs pros' 22.8 s).
entries.title: Duel edge: holder vs peeker

entries.summary: Nudging agents to save worked during the nudge, then faded in one block.
entries.title: Save rule + save kick

entries.summary: A saved rifle is worth as much as in pro CS; the per-tick discount makes the next round count only ~44%.
entries.title: Why agents don't save: the discount

entries.metric: next-round win gain from a saved rifle (ours vs pros)
entries.summary: A saved rifle is worth as much here as in pro CS; the learner just discounts the next round to ~0.44 of this one.
entries.title: Why agents don't save: the per-tick discount

entries.summary: A newer optimizer (Muon) matched Adam but gained only +2 Elo against a +15 bar, so Adam stayed.
entries.title: Muon optimizer vs Adam

entries.metric: lost CT rounds with a survivor, arm vs control
entries.summary: The value net learned to price saving (+0.041) but agents saved no more; the package was kept anyway for realism.
entries.title: Economy package with in-round gamma 0.997

entries.metric: mean win-rate gain of fresh defending exploiters (gline6)
entries.summary: A fresh opponent trained only to defend beats the agent's attack by +0.05 win rate, even as its Elo rises.
entries.title: Robustness probes, 3v3

entries.metric: Elo economy main line vs start, start's game (no-harm >= -8)
entries.summary: Teams now keep sides for 12 rounds, swap at halftime and can't see enemy money, at no measurable cost.
entries.title: Halftime, match score, hidden enemy money

entries.metric: Elo arm-control, own game, CS maps
entries.summary: Real CS2 guns (AK, M4, AWP...) with real prices gained +5 Elo; AWP kill share 0.105 matches pros' 0.107.
entries.title: Individual CS2 guns with real prices

entries.summary: Pushing agents to save worked only while pushed (+0.045), vanished a block later, and cost 7 Elo. Saving was closed.
entries.title: Save kick on the economy package

entries.metric: light-buy upgrade rate, arm vs control
entries.summary: Dropped guns can be picked up, but agents didn't learn to fetch them (0.257 vs 0.246 by chance). Harmless; kept off.
entries.title: Weapons on the ground

entries.summary: Pulling weights back toward their start did nothing (-2 Elo); the weights barely drift anyway (0.68% in 2 blocks).
entries.title: Weight anchoring (l2_init 1e-3)

entries.metric: frozen agent win rate vs bots after widening (copy vs zero-init)
entries.summary: To go from 3v3 to 5v5, trained player slots are copied; zero-filled slots left new enemies invisible (0.50 vs 0.72 win).
entries.title: 5v5 support and slot widening

entries.summary: The owner decided the goal is bots that beat pros, not bots that copy pro statistics exactly.
entries.title: Pro stats become a sanity band

entries.metric: attack win vs bots after 5e7 steps from scratch (new vs old kick)
entries.summary: A new way to bootstrap a fresh network from a trained one: 0.73 attack win vs bots after 5e7 steps; the old way got 0 kills.
entries.title: Forward-KL kickstart

entries.summary: A browser mode lets a person play against the agents with fog of war and positional sound; agents answer in 9-15 ms.
entries.title: Human play mode

entries.metric: Elo vs warm line gline4 at block 12
entries.summary: A fresh network learned fast at first but stayed 122 Elo behind the long-trained line after 12 blocks, so it was stopped.
entries.title: From-scratch restart (route K)

entries.summary: A full test run (3,251 passed) found two features that silently changed the computation order when switched off; fixed.
entries.title: Full test tier finds drifted programs

entries.summary: The friend's PC with the main GPU froze several times (one outage 27 h); fixes and a flight recorder, cause still open.
entries.title: Borrowed 2080 Ti PC keeps freezing

entries.summary: The 3v3 main line kept improving in the full economy game: +11 Elo over two blocks.
entries.title: 3v3 main line in the full economy game

entries.summary: From 224 pro matches: first enemy contact at a median 22.8 s; a T lurker in 29% of rounds.
entries.title: Pro team-role statistics

entries.metric: rounds won per 12-round half, best policy vs scripted rule
entries.summary: A simulator showed the best buy policy is simply 'buy everything every round', so no learned buyer was built.
entries.title: Learned buying (E3)

entries.summary: Flashes can now be lobbed over walls. Agents threw 70% more but still from where they see the pop. Kept for realism.
entries.title: Flash self-blind diagnosis and lob / bank flashes

entries.summary: Scripted bots with CS team roles (lurkers, splits, stacks) gave a small gain (+2, +7 on new maps) and cheaper training.
entries.title: Bot team roles as training opponents

entries.metric: Elo v5a2 vs widened start in 5v5 (3v3: -94)
entries.summary: Trained at 5v5, the agent gained +317 Elo there but lost 94 at 3v3. The owner switched the main line to 5v5.
entries.title: 5v5 test and switch of the main line

entries.summary: A full-strength imitation term drowned the RL signal: policy randomness jumped 7x and win rate fell 0.79 to 0.53.
entries.title: Flash kick v3 at coefficient 1

entries.summary: Making every team always buy full gave no gain (-4 Elo) and deleted eco rounds, so the pro-like buy rule stayed.
entries.title: 'FULL every round' buy rule, 5v5

entries.summary: At 1/33 strength the same imitation term added +4 to +8 Elo on every read, though not through better flashes.
entries.title: Fixed flash kick at 1/33 strength

entries.summary: The 5v5 line gained +52 Elo in 8 blocks; gains per two blocks shrank from +17 to +6.
entries.title: 5v5 main line blocks 3-10

entries.metric: pros' trades within 5 s (corrected minus old)
entries.summary: Player IDs rounded by a float conversion hid half the pro data's trades: the true trade rate is 25.2%, not 13.4%.
entries.title: Pro data: rounded Steam IDs

entries.metric: share of tile pairs where grid and mesh disagree (where pros fight 20.7%)
entries.summary: Our 4.4 m grid sees through about 1 in 7 lines that real CS2 walls, ledges and crates block.
entries.title: Grid sight vs real CS2 mesh sight

entries.metric: pro kill sightlines lost at 0.5 m voxels (0.125 m: 7.9%)
entries.summary: Half-metre voxels lose 42% of real pro kill sightlines; 12.5 cm voxels are needed (7.9% lost).
entries.title: S3 voxel sight resolution and multi-floor shares

entries.summary: A compiler turns CS2's own navigation files into grids at any resolution; it found 42 errors in our hand-made maps.
entries.title: Map compiler from CS2 nav files

entries.summary: All line-of-sight code now goes through one interface, and games point to shared maps instead of copying them.
entries.title: One sight interface, maps by reference

entries.summary: New training maps look far more like CS (3.7 vs 8.4 off-range stats) but gave no Elo; adopted for realism.
entries.title: Generator v3 (more CS-like maps)

entries.summary: Eight times finer sight checks cost only 1.42x per training chunk; a precomputed sight table is ~7x cheaper than today's.
entries.title: Sight cost, table sight, bot-gate noise, 2x2 bodies

entries.metric: chunk time ratio on the 2080 Ti (new speed code)
entries.summary: A lookup table replaces wall ray-marching with bit-identical play: 7% faster on the main GPU once other code was sped up.
entries.title: Exact wall-table sight backend

entries.summary: After 28 blocks the 5v5 agent is +96 Elo over its 5v5 start, still climbing ~2.5-3 Elo per block.
entries.title: 5v5 main line blocks 13-28

entries.metric: head's defence win vs bots, tile -> mesh
entries.summary: With real CS2 sightlines the agent's defence falls from 0.77 to 0.62: it learned to hold through walls the grid lacks.
entries.title: Real-mesh sight on CS maps (S1)

entries.metric: Elo head - v5a2, compiled maps (hand maps +96)
entries.summary: On maps compiled from CS2's own data the agent keeps ~90% of its margin (+86 vs +96 Elo).
entries.title: Playing on compiled CS maps

entries.metric: mean gain of fresh defending exploiters vs g5line28 (v5a2: +0.066)
entries.summary: A fresh defender still beats the agent's attack by +0.034 win rate, down from +0.066 at the start of 5v5.
entries.title: Robustness probes, 5v5

entries.metric: holder beats peeker, corrected (was read as 0.50; pros 0.657)
entries.summary: 'Holders lose' was a measurement bug; the real flaw: a peek-and-back within one 0.8 s tick can never be shot.
entries.title: Readout bug and the free one-tick peek

entries.metric: defend-ladder gain on mesh-64 (bar +0.04); CS Elo -9
entries.summary: Adding CS-like small cover to training maps didn't fix defence (+0.012 vs +0.04 bar) and cost 9 Elo; stopped.
entries.title: Fine cover and sight in generated maps (S1-train)

entries.summary: 28 blocks made the agent stronger but not more CS-like: first contact stays at 9.6 s vs pros' 22.8 s.
entries.title: Behaviour across 28 blocks

entries.metric: frames per second, 3D with Dust2 mesh
entries.summary: Replays and play now render in 3D (three.js), first person, with the real CS2 map drawn around you at ~60 fps.
entries.title: 3D viewer and 3D play

entries.metric: Elo arm-control, snap game, CS maps
entries.summary: Bots that hold angles longer did not make the agent stronger (-7 Elo); kept as an optional bot set.
entries.title: Holding bot personas

entries.summary: Rewriting hot code paths made training ~13% faster on the main GPU with exactly the same results.
entries.title: Exact speedups

entries.summary: Bots can now step diagonally like the agents; small gain (+2 Elo), no cost, adopted for realism.
entries.title: Diagonal bot movement

entries.metric: today's agent defence vs bots, flat -> real CS floors
entries.summary: Maps gained floors, ramps and drops; today's agent defends much worse on real CS heights (0.64 to 0.52).
entries.title: Heights on tiles and in the generator

entries.summary: Letting set defenders snap-shoot a quick peeker cut peek-and-back by a third; +29 Elo in the new rules, adopted.
entries.title: Snap fire

entries.summary: New plan: rebuild the game in real CS2 units and timings; today's 0.8 s decision tick is ~3.5x a human reaction.
entries.title: Plan: one metric CS core, distil once

entries.metric: ms per 0.8 s decision for 51 movement sub-steps, 5,120 bodies
entries.summary: Real CS movement at 64 Hz costs ~1 ms per decision for 5,120 bodies; physics is cheap, decisions are expensive.
entries.title: Sub-ticks, 64 Hz movement, Warp

entries.metric: share of pro stops from a run that are counter-strafes

entries.metric: minutes per seed on the 1660 Ti
entries.summary: A two-minute 1v1 training test now catches broken learning before any long GPU run.
entries.title: R1 regression check

entries.metric: chunk time ratio, obs v2 (shared encoder 1.37x update, parked)
entries.summary: A new observation and action format in real units reproduces today's game exactly; costs ~12% more per chunk.
entries.title: Interface v2

entries.metric: bugs found by two cloud reviews
entries.summary: Cloud sessions wrote CS-style movement, collision, sight and reaction-time modules; two reviews found 18 bugs.
entries.title: Metric-core modules by cloud sessions

entries.summary: Removing the within-round discount did not help (-3.3 Elo).
entries.title: In-round gamma 1.0

entries.metric: bot rounds per hour on 4 servers
entries.summary: A real CS2 server now runs at 10x speed (~1,140 bot rounds/h on 4 servers) and can be read and steered.
entries.title: A real CS2 server as referee

entries.summary: Dropping an extra value-network pass cost ~4 Elo (within no-harm) and made training 11-14% faster.
entries.title: Drop the PPG critic-only pass

entries.metric: Elo student - teacher, CS maps, zero-shot
entries.summary: Copying the agent into the new interface loses only 13 Elo; extra imitation during later RL only slows it.

entries.summary: The new main line (CS-like maps, snap fire) still gains ~4-5 Elo per block.
entries.title: v3 main line progress
